tech.title: OpenAI's ‘shepherds' affirm blockbuster physics result
tech.summary: Experts appointed by OpenAI have verified OpenAI's proof of the existence of the quantum Yang-Mills theory, a vital foundation for the Standard Model of particle physics. OpenAI created a committee to supervise the proof's release after backlash it received when it released a flood of more than 700 AI-generated proofs on a single day in October. This shepherding approach has riled some mathematicians, who see it as an act of needless gatekeeping. The experts do not claim to fully understand the proof yet, as it is too lengthy and complicated for human minds to immediately grasp.

tech.title: Handing over humanity
tech.summary: Some AI experts believe that once we achieve superintelligence, humans will be permanently disempowered, and we shall all be ruled by an AI god. This might not be such a desirable outcome, as humans have a natural desire for freedom. The arrangement will probably not work, as keeping power responsive to human needs has required checks developed over centuries, sustained by repeated feedback from the real world and correction, and there's no reason to keep that equilibrium stable once humans have surrendered all control. Humans have the ability now to steer the technology in a way that will not lead to a complete replacement of human judgment.

webdev.title: What Is Eval-Driven Development? How to Improve AI Agents
webdev.summary: Tweaking agents by hand-testing a few prompts makes it hard to tell whether a change helped or hurt, since outputs vary and several answers can be correct. LangChain proposes a test-driven-style loop: write a pass/fail spec for one behavior, build the dataset and evaluator before the change, then compare experiments example by example, since a higher average can hide regressions. It also urges keeping a held-out set to catch overfitting and running evals in CI and on live traffic, feeding production failures back into the dataset.

webdev.title: How we cut Next.js memory from ~5GB to ~1GB: the react-query timer holding every SSR request
webdev.summary: Zepto's Next.js pods sat at about 5 GB because react-query v3 starts a multi-minute cache timer for every query rendered on the server, and Node ties each timer to the request's AsyncLocalStorage context, keeping every finished request in memory. Building server-side queries with an infinite cache time stopped the timers and dropped pods to about 1.2 GB, and the same trap still applies on v5 when hooks set an explicit gcTime. The fix also exposed that autoscaling had been driven by the leak, so teams fixing memory issues should watch replica counts and latency afterward.

data.title: Fact-Checking at Scale: Building a More Accurate and Efficient Synopsis Factuality System

data.title: Parquet's Revised Modular Footer Proposal: Row Groups Stop Being Physical Boundaries
data.summary: A revised Apache Parquet proposal would replace monolithic Thrift footers with independently readable metadata modules encoded as Parquet pages. Column chunks become contiguous page sequences, row-group metadata becomes optional, and statistics can describe arbitrary row ranges rather than fixed groups. Readers could retrieve metadata only for relevant columns, reducing planning overhead on wide tables. The redesign remains under community review and would require changes across readers and writers.

data.title: Iceberg v4 Stats-Only Fields: How Tables Store Statistics for Partition Expressions
data.summary: Apache Iceberg v4 introduces stats-only fields that store metadata for derived expressions, such as partition buckets or case-normalized strings, without materializing additional table columns. Statistics are encoded as typed fields in manifest content_stats structures, enabling expression-aware file pruning. A new file-level tight_stats flag identifies exact live-row counts and eligible bounds, improving planning and potentially enabling metadata-only computations without scanning underlying data files.

A more reliable architecture separates an ontology that translates business intent from a precision layer that enforces tested calculations, keeping the warehouse's role as a consistent source of truth.

data.title: e-means: Outperforming k-means in One-Tenth the Epochs
data.summary: Meta FAIR researchers introduced e-means, a mini-batch clustering algorithm that updates centroids using exponential moving averages instead of repeatedly processing entire datasets. Across embedding benchmarks, it achieves lower clustering loss in 1.4–2.6 epochs than traditional Lloyd's k-means reaches in 25, with reported GPU speedups of 10–45x against optimized implementations.

marketing.title: The next big creators will be experts
marketing.summary: Audiences are growing tired of polished, interchangeable creators and increasingly value experts who offer firsthand knowledge, credible stories, and informed perspectives. Brands should look beyond follower counts when choosing creators and prioritize people with deep subject expertise, a proven track record, and the ability to support their claims with evidence. Four qualities matter when evaluating expert voices: a genuine obsession with their subject, the ability to hold attention beyond short clips, transparency about sources and uncertainty, and the willingness to challenge a brand's assumptions. Pairing experienced experts with younger creators who understand modern formats can also help turn specialized knowledge into content that travels widely.

marketing.title: How to Pitch TV News with Jodi Gralnick (Former CNBC Producer)
marketing.summary: Effective TV pitching starts with matching your story to the right outlet, show, producer, and audience. TV needs strong visuals, graphics, and a relevant human guest, while digital can support deeper research, more data, and written quotes. Research each outlet and journalist before pitching, and write subject lines as headlines the outlet would actually publish. Get ahead of predictable news events by offering expert sources and unique perspectives before journalists start building their coverage. Pitches also need a timely news angle, objective audience relevance, and exclusive information, since 99% of pitches are irrelevant to the person receiving them.
